subject: MAP: performance harness & long-context KV sweep for AuroraData (close timeline)
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroradata.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: perf harness + long-context plan (timeline to close)

Samir,

Thanks again for the time this morning — excited to get AuroraData onto Redwood Dedicated for the evaluation. Per our conversation, attached is a draft MAP (PDF) that ties the evaluation milestones to a proposed close timeline. High level asks from our side:

- We run a focused perf harness that measures latency (p50/p90/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), TTFT (cold vs warm), and concurrency behavior across your target prompt distribution.
- Long-context tests at max seq lengths representative of your use: 8k, 16k, 32k (and a 64k exploratory run if feasible).
- KV cache sweep to show impact on TTFT and per-token cost when using repeated prefixes.
- Delivery: interim CSV with raw metrics, a short findings doc, and a recommendation on model/quantization profile.

Proposed timeline (can be tightened):
- 6/11: finalize test matrix (you + eval team)
- 6/12–6/16: runs (SE runs with your test keys in staging)
- 6/17: interim results snapshot
- 6/18–6/19: one focused re-run based on anomalies
- 6/22: final recap and contract markup
- target close: 6/25–6/26

Can you confirm the eval team's availability to finalize the matrix tomorrow? Rafael will share the detailed test plan once you confirm.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

----------
From: Samir Patel <samir@auroradata.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: perf harness + long-context plan (timeline to close)

Aditya — thanks, this looks good. I looped in our eval alias and Lena (tokenization lead). A few clarifications before we lock the matrix:

- We need p50/p90/p99 and also 95th percentile tokens/sec aggregated by prompt-length bucket.
- For TTFT, please capture both cold-start (first token, cold model) and warm-start (with KV cache primed) across concurrency levels.
- Concurrency: test 1, 8, 32, 64, 128 (our production spikes sit around 60–80).
- Please include memory and GPU utilization samples so our infra team can reconcile limits.

If you can share the SE test matrix today we’ll sign off and run on our side. Can we also schedule a 30-min sync on 6/12?

—Samir
Head of Platform
AuroraData

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroradata.com>, AuroraData Evaluation Team <eval@auroradata.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@auroradata.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood perf harness: detailed test matrix (attached)

Samir / team — attaching the test matrix and the perf harness runbook (auroradata-map-v1.pdf). Highlights below and what we will collect:

Test matrix overview:
- Sequence length buckets: 256, 1k, 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k (single-run 64k optional)
- Prompt size distribution: we’ll run both synthetic uniform buckets and a sampled distribution you provided (Lena, please confirm sample set).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 64, 128 requests in steady-state and short surge windows (60s).
- Model variants: base open model (FP16), int8 quantized build, and a larger context-optimized variant (if available).
- KV cache modes: off, prefix-cache (100 tokens cached), full KV (all repeated context cached).

Metrics captured (per-run):
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 end-to-end (request in -> last token out)
- TTFT: first-byte latency (time to first model token) cold vs warm
- Throughput: tokens/sec aggregated and per-worker breakdown
- GPU utilization, RAM, and decoder memory footprint samples (periodic sampling)
- Error rates and partial output counts
- Cost proxy: tokens-per-second * GPU-second consumption estimate

Warm vs cold methodology:
- Cold run = model cold start + KV empty; we will restart the worker pool between runs to approximate cold-starts.
- Warm run = steady-state with KV primed for 5-minute window; we’ll measure TTFT improvement and variance.

Acceptance criteria for handoff to commercial stage:
- p95 latency at target seq length <= 800ms for the chosen model variant (or agreed SLA)
- No P99 spikes > 3x p95 under steady-state concurrency
- KV cache yields >10% TTFT improvement for repeated prefix workloads without >10% memory tail growth

Attachments: detailed runbook includes command lines, tracing hooks, and CSV output schema. Plan to run the first batch 6/13–6/16 in your staging gst. Please confirm sample prompts.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

----------
From: Samir Patel <samir@auroradata.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraData Evaluation Team <eval@auroradata.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@auroradata.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood perf harness: detailed test matrix (attached)

Rafael — thanks for the level of detail. A couple of requests before you start:

1) Add intermediate concurrency 16 and 48 — our traffic pattern is spiky and often lands between 32 and 64.
2) For prompt distribution, please run both (a) the sampled customer prompts we uploaded to the Drive folder and (b) a synthetic heavy-end distribution skewed to 8k–16k tails.
3) Can you log cold-start CPU+init time separately (we need to reconcile with our autoscaler metrics)?

We’ll aim to have the eval team run mirrored tests on our side in parallel; timeline still OK for a close in the 6/25–6/26 window provided there are no regressions.

—Samir

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroradata.com>, AuroraData Evaluation Team <eval@auroradata.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Interim perf snapshot and notes (csv attached)

Team — sharing an interim CSV with raw metrics (perf-results-20260618.csv) and a short summary below. This is the first-pass run Rafael executed in our staging environment using AuroraData's sample prompts. Key takeaways:

- Concurrency behavior: steady-state throughput scales linearly from 1 -> 32. At 64 we see ~12% queuing overhead; at 128 the p99 latency increases sharply (3.2x p95) indicating GPU saturation in current config.
- Long-context impacts:
  - 8k: p95 within target, tokens/sec ~85% of baseline (1k)
  - 16k: p95 increases ~1.6x vs 8k, tokens/sec drops ~35%
  - 32k: p95 shows heavy tail; runs hit memory pressure and occasional OOMs on a 48GB GPU. Recommend either model variant with memory-optimized kernels or a sharded serving config for >32k.
- TTFT & KV cache: enabling prefix KV cache reduced median TTFT by ~18% across 8k/16k buckets; cold TTFT still dominated by model setup time (~220ms additional on cold worker). KV cache increases RAM usage by ~6% on average, with max observed tail at 11% during 32k runs.
- Cost proxy: tokens/sec per GPU-second improved with KV caching for repeated-context workloads; not beneficial for wholly unique prompts.

Anomalies and next steps:
- 32k instability: we’ll run a targeted memory-profile with expanded sampling and try quantized variant to reduce memory footprint.
- Surge testing: will add concurrency levels 16 and 48 per Samir’s ask.

Attached: perf-results-20260618.csv (raw runs), kv-cache-sweep.log (trace). We’ll schedule a quick 20-min sync tomorrow to review the CSV and coordinate the targeted re-run.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment placeholders:
- perf-results-20260618.csv (CSV: run_id,seq_len,concurrency,p50_ms,p90_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,ttft_ms,tokens_per_sec,gpu_util,ram_mb,errors)
- kv-cache-sweep.log (plain text traces)

From: Samir Patel <samir@auroradata.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraData Evaluation Team <eval@auroradata.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interim perf snapshot and notes (csv attached)

All — really useful work, thank you. Quick notes:

- Please prioritize the targeted 32k runs with expanded sampling and the quantized variant. If OOMs persist, propose a sharded approach and include an A/B cost delta.
- We want one final run matching our production prompt distribution (not synthetic) before we sign. Can you run that on 6/19 and share the resulting CSV by EOD so our infra team can validate?
- Small ask on rollouts: share a canary rollout plan (A/B weight, metrics to watch, rollback threshold). We’ll need that in the final MAP before procurement signs.

If we get the final CSV and canary plan by 6/19–6/20, we’re still aligned with a contractual close by 6/26.

Thanks — Samir
Head of Platform
AuroraData
